paper.title_en: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
paper.abstract_en: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.
